\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Savitch ARM --- Correct: Introduction}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM.Correct}.

\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Savitch ARM --- Correct: Results}

\begin{definition}[Four languages associated with a machine]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.decs}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.decs}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.acceptLang, Complexity.Codec.initLang, Complexity.Codec.stepLang, Complexity.inputLenLang, Turing.FinNDTM}
For a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean alphabet, define a family
of four languages indexed by $j\in\{0,1,2,3\}$: the language at index $0$ is the
input-length language, and those at indices $1$, $2$, and $3$ are respectively the
initialization, acceptance, and step languages associated with $N$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Language membership indicators]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.orcN}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.orcN}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.decs, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
For a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean alphabet, define a
Boolean-valued function on indices $j\in\{0,1,2,3\}$ and Boolean lists $V$ that is true
exactly when $V$ belongs to the language at index $j$ in the associated family of four
languages.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Encoded Step Relation Agreement]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rel_orcN}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rel_orcN}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.StepRel, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.decs, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.orcN, Complexity.LogProg.indicator_eq_decide, Turing.FinNDTM}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine, let $x$ be a bit string, and let
$s$ be a natural number. The relation obtained by querying the machine’s step-decider
oracle on the encoded input consisting of $x$, the binary representations of two
configuration codes, and $s$ agrees with the step relation defined by membership of that
same encoding in the machine’s step language.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Initial-code oracle characterization]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.initO_orcN}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.initO_orcN}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.initLang, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.InitO, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.decs, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.orcN, Complexity.LogProg.indicator_eq_decide, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine, let $x$ be a bit string, and let
$s,u\in\mathbb{N}$. The initial-code oracle accepts the encoding $\langle x,\langle
\mathrm{bits}(u),\mathrm{bits}(s)\rangle\rangle$ if and only if that encoding belongs to
the language of valid initial configuration codes for $N$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Acceptance-checker characterization]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.accO_orcN}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.accO_orcN}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.acceptLang, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.AccO, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.decs, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.orcN, Complexity.LogProg.indicator_eq_decide, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, let $x$
be a finite Boolean string, and let $s,v$ be natural numbers. The acceptance checker for
$N$, when given the nested pair encoding of $x$, the binary expansion of $v$, and the
binary expansion of $s$, returns true if and only if that encoded string belongs to the
language of encodings of accepting configurations of $N$ on input $x$ within window
radius $s$ and with configuration code $v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Machine-dependent natural number]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.bigE}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.bigE}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.codeK, Turing.FinNDTM}
For a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean alphabet and natural
numbers $k$ and $c$, define $E(N,k,c)=k+c+1+2C(N)+\bigl(|Q|+2+9t\bigr)$, where $C(N)$ is
the code parameter of $N$, $Q$ is its finite state set, and $t$ is its number of work
tapes.
\end{definition}

}
\label{Complexity.NSPACE_poly_subset_PSPACE}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.acceptLang_mem, Complexity.Codec.initLang_mem, Complexity.Codec.stepLang_mem, Complexity.LOGSPACE_subset_PSPACE, Complexity.LogProg.AHalt.mono, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.accO_orcN, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.bigE, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.codeWidth_le, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.configBound_le, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.decs, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.initO_orcN, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mem_iff_reach, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.orcN, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.radius_le, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rel_orcN, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.savitch_halts, Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_pspace_val, Complexity.LogProg.indicator_eq_decide, Complexity.NSPACE, Complexity.PSPACE, Complexity.indicator_indexLang_pairEncode, Complexity.inputLenLang, Complexity.inputLenLang_mem, Turing.pairEncode}

For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, $\mathrm{NSPACE}(n\mapsto n^k+1)\subseteq\mathrm{PSPACE}$.
\end{theorem}

\proofstep
  {Complexity.NSPACE_poly_subset_PSPACE}
  {direct}
  {Sav70}
  {pdf-c8033d2fd705-p003-b005,
    pdf-c8033d2fd705-p004-b001}
\uses{Complexity.NPSPACE, Complexity.NSPACE_poly_subset_PSPACE, Complexity.PSPACE}
\difficulty{4}
Every language decidable by a finite nondeterministic Turing machine using space at most
a constant multiple of $n^c+1$ for some $c\in\mathbb{N}$ belongs to $	ext{PSPACE}$, the
union over $d\in\mathbb{N}$ of deterministic space classes using at most a constant
multiple of $n^d+1$.
\end{theorem}
